Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

how much adverb and pronoun

what amount?

also as much as, how much?, how great, how much of, so much, so much of

classical

Sen. Ep. 76.5: ‘quantum’ inquis ‘prōficiam?’ quantum temptāveris
Hor. Ep. 1.7.16: at tū, quantum vīs, tolle

quantum

neuter of quantus, as a pronoun (with a genitive) or an adverb · Wiktionary

how much? as much as

With a genitive, how much of: quantum morae, how much delay. Answered by tantum, which takes the genitive the same way (tantum cibī, so much food): quantum … tantum, as much … so much (Cic. Fam. 16.2.1).

Other words

  • quantus, quanta, quantum — how great? how big? how much …!

    adjective, interrogative, relative and exclamatory · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.5.43: ō quī complexūs et gaudia quanta fuērunt; Traupman 330 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Answered by tantus (see “such”).

  • quantī — how much? (price, value)

    genitive of value · also used · classical · Mart. 14.218.1: dīc quotus et quantī cupiās cēnāre · Wiktionary

    Of price: see “how much is it?”.

Examples

  • vēscere, sōdēs. — jam satis est. — at tū, quantum vīs, tolle. — benignē.

    Do eat, please. — I’ve had enough. — Well, take as much as you like. — No, thank you.Hor. Ep. 1.7.15–16

  • ‘quantum’ inquis ‘prōficiam?’ quantum temptāveris

    “How much shall I gain?” you ask. As much as you trySen. Ep. 76.5

  • nōn quantum vīs sed quantum capis hauriendum est

    you should take in not as much as you want but as much as you can holdSen. Ep. 108.2

  • quantum mē dīligis, tantum fac ut valeās

    as much as you love me, so much see that you get wellCic. Fam. 16.2.1

  • ō quī complexūs et gaudia quanta fuērunt

    oh, what embraces there were, and how much joy!Hor. S. 1.5.43

  • incrēdibile est, quantum morae lēctiōnī festīnātiōne adjiciātur

    it is unbelievable how much delay hurrying adds to readingQuint. 1.1.32

  • tantum cibī et pōtiōnis adhibendum ut reficiantur vīrēs, nōn opprimantur

    only so much food and drink should be taken as restores one’s strength without crushing itCic. Sen. 36

  • tantum nivis fodiendum atque ēgerendum fuit

    so much snow had to be dug out and carried awayLiv. 21.37.1

See also how many, how much is it?, such, how.
